entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv6474"/><div sID="gen9920" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv6474"/><hi type="bold">2. longeth--</hi>most intensely (<reference osisRef="Gen.31.30">Ge 31:30</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.17.12">Psa 17:12</reference>).<div eID="gen9920" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen9921" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">fainteth--</hi>exhausted with desire.<div eID="gen9921" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen9922" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">courts--</hi>as tabernacles (<reference osisRef="Ps.84.1">Psa 84:1</reference>)--the whole building.<div eID="gen9922" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen9923" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">crieth out--</hi>literally, "sings for joy"; but here, and <reference osisRef="Lam.2.19">La 2:19</reference>, expresses an act of sorrow as the corresponding noun (<reference osisRef="Ps.17.1">Psa 17:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.61.2">61:2</reference>).<div eID="gen9923" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen9924" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">heart and ... flesh--</hi>as in <reference osisRef="Ps.63.1">Psa 63:1</reference>. <div eID="gen9924" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 2. longeth-- most intensely ( Ge 31:30 ; Psa 17:12 ). fainteth-- exhausted with desire. courts-- as tabernacles ( Psa 84:1 )--the whole building. crieth out-- literally, "sings for joy"; but here, and La 2:19 , expresses an act of sorrow as the corresponding noun ( Psa 17:1 ; 61:2 ). heart and ... flesh-- as in Psa 63:1 .

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv6475"/><div sID="gen9925" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv6475"/><hi type="bold">3. thine altars--</hi>that is, of burnt offering and incense, used for the whole tabernacle. Its structure afforded facilities for sparrows and swallows to indulge their known predilections for such places. Some understand the statement as to the birds as a comparison: "as they find homes, so do I desire thine altars," &c. <div eID="gen9925" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv6478"/><div sID="gen9929" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv6478"/><hi type="bold">6. valley of Baca--</hi>or, "weeping." Through such, by reason of their dry and barren condition, the worshippers often had to pass to Jerusalem. As they might become wells, or fountains, or pools, supplied by refreshing rain, so the grace of God, by the exercises of His worship, refreshes and revives the hearts of His people, so that for sorrows they have "rivers of delight" (<reference osisRef="Ps.36.8">Psa 36:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.46.4">46:4</reference>). <div eID="gen9929" type="x-p"/>
